analysis:
The PR only adds a changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen-prefill-interleave.md, lines 1-3) and one documentation table row (docs/architecture/inference.md, head line 1389) for `decodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks`. The row says the value is 4 for the Qwen 3.5 family and 0 otherwise, sourced from `EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift` (`qwenDecodeStepsBetweenPrefillChunks`). The supplied evidence contains no code change, so no control, key handling, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing path changed here.

The documented behavior is a scheduling change: decode-only steps run between prompt chunks. It could affect availability and latency (T-010, T-029, ADV-002 starvation concerns) and the prefill/decode timing profile. The changelog reports about a 21% longer first-token time for the long prompt, which is a fairness trade-off rather than a vulnerability. Any timing-oracle effect on prefix-cache hits (T-041 / SEC-035) is speculative and not evidenced; the cache scoping, HMAC lookup tags and TTL are not touched.

The actual Swift implementation (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift and the CBv2 scheduler) was not supplied. The next pass should check that the new setting does not bypass step budgets, memory admission or cancellation handling during interleaved prefill. The diff is documentation-only, so I found no security regression and no threat-model gap that requires an update.
